correctness.rationale: One-step SIR on a rooted tree equals independent bond percolation with infection generations given by root-path distance. The exact Bernsteins reconstruct E[C(F)], and the derivative is a positive Bernstein-weighted sum of adjacent conditional means. Standalone pure-Python Prüfer enumeration checks all 85 root-preserving isomorphism classes through n=7 and all masks, comparing a complete 85-row rational certificate byte-for-byte. Nonnegative differences cover all n<=6 and 46 n=7 types; two exceptional polynomial identities are additionally proved by independent binomial event conditioning. Their endpoint derivatives are -1/7 and -3/7; unique internal maxima follow from Descartes polynomial transforms. No infinite-order claims or reliance on numerical-only evidence.

Full-source comparisons found no implication or stronger result giving those finite sharp assertions; these conclusions are best-knowledge, not a proof of universal publication priority.

value.rationale: The primary literature raises the mathematically motivated question of nonmonotonic cumulative burden at the epidemic peak but offers large-network simulations, not a sharp finite graph threshold. Determining that six rooted-tree vertices never suffice and that exactly two seven-vertex root types do, with exact peak polynomials and unique thresholds, is a natural complete initial-obstruction classification. It clarifies a model-statistic boundary and supplies checkable finite epidemic benchmarks; no downstream paper-sized theorem or large numerical magnitude is assumed.
